history.period: 15th century (matha tradition dates its lineage to c. 1300 AD)
history.summary: NOT A TEMPLE — a matha (monastery): keep-or-drop decision needed. Shree Siddaganga Matha is a prominent Lingayat (Veerashaiva) monastery at Kyathasandra near Tumakuru, founded in the 15th century by Sri Haradanahalli Gosala Siddeshwara Swamigalu. Its most famous pontiff, Sri Sri Shivakumara Swami (born Shivanna, 1 April 1907), headed the matha from 1941 until his death on 21 January 2019, building the Sri Siddaganga Education Society (~125-132 institutions) and a free gurukula for ~9,000-10,000 poor children with food, education and shelter regardless of caste or religion; he was honoured with the Padma Bhushan (2015) and Karnataka Ratna (2007) and called the 'Walking God'. Current head per Wikipedia: Sri Siddalinga Swami. The matha's gurukula and annadana (free meals for pilgrims) continue. Town correction: the matha is at Kyathasandra (post office Kyathasandra), not Tumkur town itself. Opening hours given are typical for the campus (verify locally).

name: Siddaganga Mutt
town_description: Kyathasandra is a village suburb about 6 km from Tumakuru city on the Bengaluru-Tumakuru highway (NH-48), PIN 572104. It is best known as the seat of the Siddaganga Matha, which draws devotees, students and visitors from across Karnataka.
